idiom_name: struct tags read by a reflection-based mapper (database/sql, sqlx, GORM)
implementation_notes: Go's realisation is idiomatic rather than framework-shaped: entities are plain structs and the mapping metadata is the struct tag (db:"email_address", gorm:"column:email_address;not null") that a reflection-based mapper reads once and caches - sqlx's StructScan, GORM's schema parser, or code generated by sqlc. database/sql alone already keeps the entity dumb: the scan target list in the query function is the mapping, so even without an ORM the struct contains no persistence code. Hand-written scanning stays justified whenever the query shape matters more than the table shape.
pitfalls: Reflection sees exported fields only: an unexported field is silently ignored by most mappers.
Tags are string literals - a typo fails at runtime with a missing-destination-field error, so keep a query smoke test over each mapped struct.
Lazily built metadata caches live behind the mapper (sync.Map / once); mapping state shared across goroutines must be initialised safely.
